Jia De Guzman reflects on Alas’ journey
results.description: THE twists and turns that Alas Pilipinas went through in the first leg of the 6th SEA V.Cup eventually became part of a bigger journey that culminated in a historic silver-medal finish. Team captain Jia De Guzman reflected on the team’s struggles and setbacks after Alas Pilipinas secured the Philippines’ first-ever silver medal in the SEA V.Cup. “So the struggle we went through in the first leg? All of it was necessary. The losses, the mistakes, the moments where things didn’t click—it was all part of becoming a better team,” De Guzman wrote on Instagram. “We needed those experiences to learn, build chemistry, and understand what we’re capable of.” The Philippines overcame a gritty Indonesia side, 25-13, 23-25, 25-19, 33-31, last Sunday at the Chiang Mai Gymnasium in Thailand to finish second in the tournament. For De Guzman, the difficult first leg—which saw Alas go winless—was not a setback but an important part of the team’s development. “Every strong team in the world was once given the space to make mistakes, experience losses, and learn from them. We’re no different,” she wrote. “This silver is a beautiful reminder that growth takes time, patience, and a willingness to embrace every part of the journey.” The historic silver marked the Philippines’ first-ever runner-up finish in the SEA V.Cup in both the men’s and women’s divisions. The Alas women had previously collected a string of bronze medals in the regional tournament before finally breaking through with silver in the 2026 edition. “So proud of how far we’ve come, and even more excited for how much more we can become,” De Guzman said. She also thanked her teammates and supporters for standing by the squad throughout its difficult campaign. “Thank you to every member of this team for all your hard work and dedication. Also to everyone out there who has given us unconditional love and support.” De Guzman has also been vocal about the need for changes and reforms concerning national team athletes. She skipped the 2026 Asian Volleyball Confederation (AVC) Women’s Cup in June, where the Philippines was led by veteran Alyssa Valdez and finished eighth.
